A calendar-update failure therefore propagates as a tRPC error after the guests are already persisted, and a retry hits the uniqueGuests filter (`!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`) which yields an empty array and throws BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', so the client cannot reconcile — a real non-atomic-write/failed-retry defect visible in the dif

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in addGuests.handler.ts that guests are first persisted to the database via prisma.booking.update (lines 87-101), then calendar synchronization happens via eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees (line 165), and finally emails are sent. If updateCalendarAttendees fails, the function throws an error but the guests are already committed to the database. On retry, the uniqueGuests filter (lines 68-72) will exclude these already-added guests, making reconciliation impossible. This is a real transactional consistency bug where partial state can be left in the database.
